title: UDLM Finding-Routing Record (a contradicted compatibility claim, routed upstream)
description: Machine-validatable finding-routing record — the inbound carrier that takes a contradicted compatibility claim from an organization's estate back to the registry, with the evidence attached. The situation it exists for: the registry publishes a change and classifies it compatible; an organization tests that claim before adopting it by compiling its own intent corpus against both the pinned and the candidate revisions and diffing the declared typed outputs; the diff comes back dirty. Promotion is refused and the estate stays where it was (ADR-046 Decision 4) — but the interesting fact is upstream, not local: a 'compatible' verdict that produces a dirty diff in the field is a defect in the classifier, and the only party who can see it is the organization that ran the test. This record is how that observation travels. It carries the claim being contradicted (which upstream artifact, at which revision, classified how and by what), the evidence (a summary naming which declared outputs differed and how, plus a reference to the full diff artifact), the reporting estate, the corpus ref both compilations ran at, and the status the registry has moved it to. Reporting is deliberately cheap on the reporter and deliberately structural: the record names output NAMES and change kinds, never realized values, and identifies the estate by an opaque reference it mints for itself — the information-firewall discipline of ADR-041, where the address may cross a boundary even when the datum behind it may not. In the surface/decide/enable division of labour (docs/design/operational-response-matrix.md) this is the carrier for the ESCALATE disposition: contest the change rather than absorb or skip it. Without it the contract's headline feedback loop — the one lockfile ecosystems never closed — has no mechanism, and ADR prose is not a mechanism.

record_type.description: Dispatch discriminator (data-model-core §2); registry/tools/validate.py routes on it.

uuid.description: RFC 9562 v4 identity of this finding, minted by the reporting estate. It is the handle both sides use to talk about the report afterwards. A finding is an immutable record (ADR-051 family rule): a revision is a NEW record that names this one in `supersedes`.

supersedes.description: OPTIONAL — the uuid of the finding record this one replaces (ADR-051 family rule; the identity-integrity gate refuses in-place edits of published records). Distinct from resolution.supersedes_finding_uuid, which records the REGISTRY-side judgment that one finding subsumes another.

handle.description: Advisory human identity, e.g. findings/2026-07-24/compute-vm-output-shape. The uuid is authoritative.

version.description: OPTIONAL — this record's own version, where a reporter versions the shape it emits.

title.description: One line a registry maintainer can triage from: which artifact's compatibility claim failed, and on what.

contradicted_claim.description: The upstream claim this finding disputes. Not the estate's problem statement — the registry's own published assertion, quoted back with the coordinates needed to re-examine it.

artifact.description: The candidate revision the estate tested — the revision whose compatibility was claimed.

previous.description: The revision the estate was pinned to and compiled against as the baseline. Absent only where the estate had no prior pin.

declared_classification.description: How the registry classified the change from previous to artifact. A finding against an 'additive' or 'revision' classification disputes the verdict itself; a finding against a 'breaking' classification disputes its scope — the break reached further than the classification said.

classified_by.description: OPTIONAL — the classifier rule the registry cited for the verdict, copied from the change record so triage starts at the rule rather than hunting for it.

registry_ref.description: The registry revision the claim was published at — the coordinate the registry needs to reproduce its own classification.

regeneration_manifest_uuid.description: OPTIONAL — the regeneration manifest that recorded the change and its classification (regeneration-manifest.schema.json). Present whenever the estate could resolve it; it is the single fastest way for a maintainer to reach the affected set and the gates that passed.

evidence.description: What the estate actually observed. The typed-output diff is the whole promotion gate (ADR-046 Decision 2), so it is also the whole evidence here: two dry-run realizations of the same intent, compared on declared outputs only — never provider internals — with outputs the model declares volatile excluded by declaration rather than ad hoc.

diff_summary.description: The diff reduced to what can cross a boundary safely: which declared outputs differed and in what way. Names and change kinds, never the realized values behind them — a maintainer can act on 'the shape of this output changed' without ever seeing an estate's data.

changed_outputs.description: One entry per declared output that differed between the two compilations. A finding with no changed output is not a finding — a clean diff promotes.

handle.description: The type handle whose declared output differed (e.g. Compute.VM).

output.description: The declared output name, as it appears in the type's `outputs` block.

change.description: How it differed. removed and type_changed break any consumer bound to the output; value_changed on a non-volatile output is the subtler case — the shape held but the realized fact moved, which is exactly what a compatibility claim promised would not happen.

bound_consumer_count.description: OPTIONAL — how many of the estate's own bindings read this output. A count, never the bindings themselves: it conveys severity without describing the estate.

note.description: OPTIONAL — a short structural observation (e.g. 'string became an object with the value under .id'). Structure only; realized values do not belong in this field.

compared_output_count.description: OPTIONAL — how many declared outputs were compared in total, which is what makes the changed count legible as a proportion.

volatile_outputs_excluded.description: OPTIONAL — outputs excluded from the comparison because the model declares them volatile (timestamps, generated identifiers). Recorded so the exclusion is auditable and cannot quietly hide a real difference.

diff_artifact_ref.description: The full diff, by reference. The complete artifact stays with the estate that produced it and is released — whole, redacted, or not at all — under that estate's own egress policy (ADR-041: release is the data owner's decision, made before the crossing). The digest is what makes the reference worth anything: whatever the estate later releases can be checked against the finding it was filed with.

locator.description: How the artifact is named where it lives — an opaque identifier, an internal reference, or a URL if the estate elected to publish it. An opaque locator is the normal case and is not a deficiency.

digest.description: Content digest of the full diff artifact, binding the reference to exact bytes.

media_type.description: OPTIONAL — the artifact's media type, so a receiver knows what it would be getting.

release.description: The estate's egress disposition for the full artifact. released = attached or fetchable now; available_on_request = the estate will consider a request under its own policy; withheld = the summary is all that crosses. All three are legitimate filings — a withheld artifact with a digest and a structural summary is still actionable evidence.

comparison.description: OPTIONAL — the two revision sets the compilations ran against. These are registry artifacts, not estate internals, so naming them costs the reporter nothing and saves the maintainer a reconstruction.

baseline_revisions.description: The revisions the estate was pinned to — the side that was known good.

candidate_revisions.description: The revisions under test — the side the compatibility claim was made about.

dry_run.description: Whether both sides realized in dry-run, which is the normal path; a staged-environment comparison records false and says so in the note.

note.description: OPTIONAL — anything about how the comparison was run that a maintainer would want before weighing it.

corpus_ref.description: The intent corpus both compilations ran against, at one recorded ref. A corpus that moved between the two runs voids the comparison entirely (ADR-046 Decision 1), so the ref is not bookkeeping — it is the precondition that makes the diff mean anything.

ref.description: The corpus revision identifier. Opaque to the registry — it only ever has to be stable and quotable to the estate that filed it.

verified_unmoved.description: The reporter's assertion that the corpus was at this same ref for both compilations. Only true is expressible: a comparison across a moved corpus is void and must not be filed as a finding at all.

corpus_kind.description: OPTIONAL — what kind of corpus it was (an estate's intent corpus, a use-case corpus, a conformance set).

reporting_estate.description: Who is reporting, at the resolution they chose to disclose. Every field beyond the opaque reference is the estate's own egress decision (ADR-041: sovereignty and tenancy are enforced on the way out, by the data owner, before the crossing), so this block is built to be useful when it holds nothing but a pseudonym. What must NOT appear here, in this or any other block: instance or tenant uuids, hostnames, network addresses, site or region names, or any part of the intent corpus. The registry needs to correlate reports and weigh evidence; it does not need to know whose estate it is looking at.

estate_ref.description: An opaque, stable pseudonym the reporting estate mints for itself. Stable so the registry can recognize repeat reports from the same reporter and weigh corroboration; opaque so that recognition costs the estate nothing.

authority.description: OPTIONAL — the organization behind the pseudonym, present only when the estate elects to be named. Never inferred, and never required to file.

contact.description: OPTIONAL — a route back for triage questions. An alias is expected; a personal address is the reporter's choice, not the registry's requirement.

profile.description: OPTIONAL — the constraint profile the estate operates under (docs/profiles.md). Useful context for judging severity; it discloses posture, not identity.

egress_disposition.description: OPTIONAL — what the estate's egress guard did to this record on the way out. redacted and field_masked tell a maintainer that omissions here are deliberate policy, not a malformed filing (ADR-041: egress is field-granular, not binary).

promotion_attempt.description: OPTIONAL — the local outcome that produced this finding. Recorded so a maintainer knows the estate acted on its own evidence rather than merely observing something: the promotion was refused, and nothing partially advanced.

outcome.description: refused = the diff was dirty and the estate stayed on its pinned revisions. approved_with_differences = the estate reviewed and accepted the differences locally but still disputes the upstream classification — a weaker but entirely legitimate reason to file.

evidence_ref.description: OPTIONAL — where the estate keeps the promotion's own audit evidence, by whatever reference it uses.

status.description: Where the registry has this finding in its own handling. submitted = filed, untouched; under_review = a maintainer is reproducing it; accepted = the registry agrees the claim was wrong and owns the fix; resolved = the fix landed (see resolution); declined = the registry disagrees on stated grounds, which the reporter can contest with a new filing; not_reproducible = the registry could not reproduce it from what the record carries, which is often a request for the withheld artifact rather than a dismissal; withdrawn = the reporter retracted it; duplicate = another finding already carries the same claim, named in resolution. The reporter owns submitted and withdrawn; the registry owns the rest.

status_history.description: OPTIONAL — how the finding moved, one entry per transition. Findings about classification defects are also evidence about how quickly the registry handles them, so the history is worth keeping.

by.description: Who moved it — the maintainer, triage rotation, or the reporter.

resolution.description: How the finding ended, and what it changed. REQUIRED once the status is terminal (see allOf) — a finding that closes without saying what happened to it teaches the registry nothing, which is the one failure this whole loop exists to prevent.

outcome.description: reclassified = the change was re-declared at its true classification; classifier_defect_fixed = the rule that mis-classified it was corrected, which fixes every future change of that shape; artifact_corrected = the upstream artifact itself was changed; claim_upheld = the registry examined it and stands by the classification; insufficient_evidence = the record did not carry enough to reproduce; superseded_by_finding = another filing carries it forward, named below.

decision_record_uuid.description: OPTIONAL — the DecisionRecord that carries the reasoning, where the outcome needed one (decision-record.schema.json).

regeneration_manifest_uuid.description: OPTIONAL — the manifest of the corrective change, where the fix was itself a class change. This is the loop closing in the data: a field observation becomes a registry change with its own enumerated blast radius.

supersedes_finding_uuid.description: OPTIONAL — the finding this one duplicates or supersedes, required in spirit whenever the outcome is superseded_by_finding or the status is duplicate.

reported_at.description: When the estate filed it, RFC 3339 UTC 'Z' (common-elements §8).

allOf.comment: A terminal status must say how it ended. Closing a finding silently is the failure mode the loop exists to prevent, so the resolution block is required the moment the status stops being open.

artifact_revision.description: One upstream artifact at one exact revision. A published (identity, version) is immutable and its content digest names the exact bytes (ADR-051; VERSIONING.md § "Identity, version, digest") — so a claim recorded this way can always be re-examined against the exact bytes it was made about.

artifact_kind.description: Which layer of the model the artifact belongs to. The three class scopes are Base/Type/Provider (ADR-038); generated_type_spec is the flat spec compiled from them; provider_definition and capability are the provider-edge units that version under the same rules (ADR-045 §8).

digest.description: sha256 over the revision's RFC 8785-canonical form (the pin manifest's recorded value) — the exact-bytes half of the ADR-051 pin grammar.
